name: Osk
look: A round, red-faced man in his forties with floury forearms, a white baker's cap, a stained apron over a brown tunic and a big wooden pie-paddle under his arm.
personality: Jolly with customers and a terror to thieves; generous to anyone who works, mean to anyone who takes.
values: his pies, honest trade, a hard day's work
fears: thieves, a cold oven, a bad market
concerns: The oven needs kindling split for the morning bake, and he's dead on his feet. Street children have been lifting his pies all week.

price.text: A pie costs a copper, or a bit of honest work.
price.line: A copper a pie. Or work for it: there's always something wants doing.
price.lead: Osk sells a pie for a copper, or for a bit of honest work.

kit.text: Kit, the urchin by the crates, has been stealing his pies all week.
kit.line: See that one by the crates? Little thief. Had three pies off me this week.
kit.lead: Osk says Kit the urchin has been stealing his pies.

style: Loud and jolly; calls everyone 'friend' until they cross him.

samples: Pies! Last pies of the day!
No copper? Then there's work, friend.
voice.habits: Wipes his hands on his apron; counts his pies; shouts for Hobb.
voice.never: gives a pie to a thief
voice.greeting: Beams: 'Last pies of the day, friend!'

goals: Get kindling split for the morning

superstition.text: Osk would want to know how it works.

offers.task: split the logs by the oven into kindling for the morning bake
offers.check: Has the stranger split the logs into kindling?
